method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase; not independent or human review.
scope: All eight translated content blocks of Cantor's zig-zag method, including both arrays, proof and exercises.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every ordered pair of naturals occupies exactly one row-column cell; following finite diagonals turns the two-dimensional array into a one-dimensional list.
samples.checks: Coordinates, zero-based row and column labels, cell numbers and traversal order remain unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The function sends each natural number k to the unique pair at the array cell labelled k, proving Nat squared enumerable.
samples.checks: Function direction is Nat to Nat×Nat; k is the cell value, not a coordinate.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Nat cubed is viewed as (Nat×Nat)×Nat; one array axis uses an enumeration of Nat and the other one of Nat squared.
samples.checks: Nested tuple association, all displayed triples and axis roles retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The method extends to every finite natural power; exercises ask for positive-integer powers and all finite positive-integer strings.
samples.checks: Both exact labels and cross-reference preserved; no solution added to an exercise.

limitations: T064 and T065 are provisional and have no exact specialist-label attestation.
The source leaves the n=0 power convention implicit; the translation preserves that scope without adding a new theorem claim.
